# Temple Scroll Column 37 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** 11QT (Cave 11), Col. 37 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**37:1** And the city that I shall consecrate, setting My name and My temple in it — it shall be holy and clean.

**37:2** And nothing unclean shall be in it; and everything that is in it shall be clean.

**37:3** And everything that enters it shall be clean; and everything that goes out from it shall be clean.

**37:4** And all wine that enters it shall be clean; and all oil that enters it shall be clean.

**37:5** And every food that enters it shall be clean; no unclean food shall be brought into it.

**37:6** And the skins of the animals that are slaughtered in it — they shall be clean; and you may use them for any sacred purpose.

**37:7** And you shall not bring into My city the skin of any animal slaughtered outside it — even if it is clean — for it has not been slaughtered in My temple city.

**37:8** And you shall not defile My city with any skin of an animal that has not been slaughtered before Me.

**37:9** For as the city is holy, so also must everything that is in it be holy; and as the temple is holy, so must the city that surrounds it be holy.

**37:10** And you shall not bring into the city any unclean thing — no unclean beast and no unclean bird.

**37:11** And all wine and oil and every food that enters the city — it shall all be clean.

**37:12** And you shall not bring into it the skin of any unclean animal, and you shall not work with it in the city.

**37:13** For the city is holy to the LORD your God; and I have set My name upon it and My temple in its midst.

**37:14** And it shall be holy and clean and pure before Me for all generations.

**37:15** And nothing abominable shall be found in it; for it is the dwelling place of My name.

**37:16** And I the LORD am its God; and I shall dwell in it forever.

---

*EMET notes: Column 37 extends temple holiness to the entire city. The skin regulations (vv. 6-8, 12) are distinctive to 11QT: only skins from animals slaughtered within the city may be used there. The theological grounding is repeated: the city shares the temple's holiness because God dwells in both.*
